queries.title: Marcus thermoneutral barrier is the SymmetryFactor β=1/2 surface height
queries.chemicalQuestion: At equal force constants and thermoneutral driving force, is the Marcus forward barrier the height of the SymmetryFactor equal-curvature reactant surface at its β = 1/2 crossing coordinate?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both theories describe the same classical two-parabola crossing. SymmetryFactor computes the equal-curvature crossing coordinate as 1/2; Marcus reports the barrier as the reactant surface energy at that crossing. The delivered kernel tie-back identifies the SymmetryFactor coordinate with the kernel coordinate, and the kernel barrier is definitionally the Marcus barrier. The query asks whether the two theories report the same physical barrier height, not merely a similar notation.

queries.title: Kasha conformance is a Marcus barrier bound under the hic premise

queries.title: Is the bimolecular quenching rate a Marcus rate?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the Stern–Volmer bimolecular quenching rate constant k_q the Marcus rate of the quenching step at the same driving force and reorganization energy?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both theories are kinetic: Marcus gives an electron-transfer rate k = A exp(−ΔG‡/k_B T); Stern–Volmer writes the quencher-dependent decay as k0 + k_q[Q]. If the quenching step is an electron transfer, k_q should be a Marcus rate, so a statement-level bridge would identify the SV added channel with the Marcus rate at the quenching step driving force. The query asks for that bridge.

queries.title: Fluorescence/phosphorescence ratio is invariant under dynamic quenching

queries.title: Phosphorescence yield is a cascade of two quantum yields
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the FluorPhos phosphorescence yield exactly the product of the S₁→T₁ quantum yield and the T₁ radiative quantum yield?
queries.chemicalRationale: FluorPhos defines φ_P as the ISC branch times the T₁ radiative branch. The QuantumYield layer defines each branch as a parallel-channel yield. The query asks whether the cascade product is exactly the composition of the two yields.
